properties.name: The Coca-Cola Company
properties.what they did: From the 1930s its Christmas advertising, painted by Haddon Sundblom, spread the red-suited Santa Claus now seen worldwide (it was not the first drink company to use him: White Rock did from 1915).

properties.name: Macy's
properties.what they did: Its Thanksgiving Day Parade began in 1924 as a store promotion: employees marched to its Herald Square store, ending with Santa Claus, to open the Christmas shopping season.
properties.placed at: flagship store, Herald Square, New York

properties.name: Montgomery Ward
properties.what they did: Had its copywriter Robert L. May write Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer in 1939 as its own Christmas giveaway booklet; 2.4 million copies went out the first year.

properties.name: Alibaba Group
properties.what they did: From 2009 turned Singles' Day into a 24-hour online sales event; with JD.com it took a record US$139 billion in 2021.

properties.name: Amazon
properties.what they did: Invented Prime Day, a sales day for its members, first held on 15 July 2015 for the website's 20th anniversary.

properties.name: National Retail Federation (Shop.org)
properties.what they did: Ellen Davis of Shop.org, part of the National Retail Federation, coined "Cyber Monday" in a press release on 28 November 2005.

properties.name: Father's Day Council (New York Associated Men's Wear Retailers)
properties.what they did: Founded in 1938 by New York's men's wear retailers to "consolidate and systematize the commercial promotion" of Father's Day, with makers of ties, pipes and other gifts.
properties.placed at: New York (the city; no address given)

properties.name: Ishimuramanseido
properties.what they did: The Fukuoka confectioner sold marshmallows to men on 14 March 1977 as "Marshmallow Day"; Japan's National Confectionery Industry Association made it White Day, an "answer day" to Valentine's Day, in 1978.

properties.name: Cleveland confectioners' committee (C. C. Hartzell)
properties.what they did: Twelve Cleveland confectioners chaired by candymaker C. C. Hartzell planned the first Sweetest Day in 1921.

properties.name: National Confectioners Association
properties.what they did: In 1937 launched a movement across the candy industry to rank Sweetest Day with Mother's Day, Father's Day and Valentine's Day.

properties.name: Lotte
properties.what they did: Promoted Pepero Day from 1997; by 2012 half its yearly Pepero revenue came from that day.

properties.name: KFC Japan
properties.what they did: Its 1974 campaign "Kentucky for Christmas" made a KFC meal at Christmas a national custom; stores take orders months ahead.

properties.name: Federated Department Stores (Fred Lazarus Jr.; now Macy's, Inc.)
properties.what they did: Its head, Fred Lazarus Jr., urged President Roosevelt to move Thanksgiving a week earlier so the Christmas shopping season would be longer. Roosevelt did so in 1939 ('Franksgiving'), and Congress fixed it on the fourth Thursday in 1941.
properties.placed at: Columbus, Ohio, home of the Lazarus store and where Federated was organized (city point: Natural Earth populated places)

properties.name: Morozoff
properties.what they did: This Kobe confectioner brought Valentine's Day to Japan as a chocolate-giving day, with a 1936 advertisement in the English-language Japan Advertiser telling readers to give its boxed chocolates to their Valentine.
properties.placed at: Kobe, its headquarters (city point: Natural Earth populated places)

properties.name: Mary's Chocolate
properties.what they did: Held Japan's first Valentine's sale of chocolates, at a Tokyo department store in February 1958, and the next year began writing names on heart-shaped chocolates; chocolate makers' campaigns fixed the custom of women giving chocolate to men.
properties.placed at: Tokyo (city point: Natural Earth populated places)

properties.name: Edgar's Department Store (James Edgar)
properties.what they did: Its owner, James Edgar, dressed as Santa Claus in his Brockton store from December 1890 to draw shoppers' children, the first department store Santa; trains brought families from Boston and Providence to see him, and by about 1900 shop Santas were everywhere.

properties.name: Dictaphone Corporation (C. King Woodbridge)
properties.what they did: Its president, C. King Woodbridge, with the National Secretaries Association's president and a Young & Rubicam publicist, devised National Secretaries Week, first held in June 1952 with backing from office equipment makers; Dictaphone was its first sponsor.
properties.placed at: Bridgeport, Connecticut, where Dictaphone made its machines (city point: Natural Earth populated places)

properties.name: Young & Rubicam (Harry F. Klemfuss)
properties.what they did: Harry F. Klemfuss, a public relations account executive at this advertising agency, was one of the three who devised the secretaries week campaign that became National Secretaries Week in 1952.
properties.placed at: New York, the agency's headquarters (city point: Natural Earth populated places)

properties.name: The Gambrinus Company
properties.what they did: As regional importer of Corona and other Grupo Modelo beers, it launched a Cinco de Mayo advertising campaign in 1989 urging people to celebrate with Mexican beer; by 1996 its marketing manager said Corona was the first thing customers thought of for the day.
properties.placed at: San Antonio, Texas, its headquarters (city point: Natural Earth populated places)

properties.name: Grupo Modelo (maker of Corona)
properties.what they did: Named by historians as one of the leading promoters and beneficiaries of Cinco de Mayo in the United States, a minor holiday in Mexico that became a major beer-selling day north of the border from the 1980s.
properties.placed at: Mexico City, its headquarters (city point: Natural Earth populated places)

properties.name: Florists' Telegraph Delivery (FTD)
properties.what they did: From 1910 this florists' association urged people to wire flowers to distant mothers, and from 1917 the flower trade ran national Mother's Day promotions; when the day's founder, Anna Jarvis, threatened legal action over the carnation trade, FTD offered her a commission on sales, which she refused.
properties.placed at: Detroit, Michigan, where FTD was based (city point: Natural Earth populated places)
